pr.title: [Performance][GDN][Main] Reduce QKV layout copies for FLA attention
pr.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Reduce unnecessary QKV layout copies in Gated DeltaNet attention:
- Use head-first convolution output for prefill and reuse contiguous BNSD views on A5.
- Process decode and prefill convolution separately in ordinary mixed batches.
- Avoid intermediate QKV concatenation in ordinary and speculative decode.
- Make inputs contiguous before fallback L2 normalization to support head-first and sliced layouts.
### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No API or configuration changes. This optimizes internal tensor layout handling while preserving attention behavior.
### How was this patch tested?
Added and updated regression tests covering QKV layouts, mixed batches, ordinary and speculative decode, and multi-head normalization fallback:
- tests/ut/ops/test_gdn.py
- tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_decode_qkv.py
- tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_layout.py
- tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_mixed_batch.py
Ruff lint, formatting, and git diff --check passed. Python syntax checks passed before formatting.

[Performance][GDN]Skip unused device metadata copies for fused prefill (#16887)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR avoids constructing and copying unused GDN prefill metadata
tensors from host to device.

The generic GDN metadata builder previously generated six device-side
chunk metadata tensors for every prefill batch. These tensors are
required by the Triton fallback and PCP paths, but are not consumed by
the fused/AscendC prefill paths that operate on host-side metadata.

This PR:

- Adds a host-only GDN metadata builder and backend.
- Makes the six device-side chunk metadata fields optional.
- Retains only `cu_seqlens_host`, `chunk_indices_chunk64_host`, and the
optional device-side `keep_meta` in host-only paths.
- Routes Kimi and GLM KDA AscendC prefill paths to the host-only
backend.
- Selects the host-only builder for Qwen when a supported fused prefill
operator is available and PCP is disabled.
- Preserves the complete metadata builder for Triton fallback, PCP, and
310P paths.
- Avoids computing unused chunk offsets, update offsets, final indices,
large-block indices, and cumsum indices in host-only paths.
- Adds a device-type guard so CPU execution cannot accidentally dispatch
the NPU-only fused operator.

This removes six unnecessary H2D copy tasks together with the associated
tensor construction, allocation, and runtime submission overhead from
supported fused prefill paths.

The optimization mainly removes fixed metadata-processing overhead
rather than reducing the computation of the GDN prefill kernel itself.
Therefore, the relative TTFT improvement is more visible at lower
concurrency and shorter/moderate prompt lengths, while the gain is
increasingly amortized by the actual prefill computation as prompt
length or concurrency increases.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No.

The inference API and model output behavior remain unchanged. This is an
internal performance optimization for GDN/KDA prefill metadata
construction.

### Performance

End-to-end TTFT was measured with
`Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-W8A8-MXFP8-FULL-QUANT` running on single A5 card +
no-prefix-cache.

Before (ms) | TTFT After (ms) | Gain | Reduce (ms) |

[Feature][KV Cache] Support non-contiguous KV cache in hybrid models like Qwen3.5 and GQA models (#14340)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds non-contiguous KV cache support for hybrid Attention/Mamba
models on Ascend, including Qwen3.5 and GQA-based models.

The current Ascend implementation requires Attention and Mamba cache
pages to use the same page size and materializes contiguous cache views.
This wastes memory and prevents hybrid models from using independent
logical page layouts.

This PR:

- Supports independent Attention and Mamba KV cache page sizes.
- Creates stride-based cache views for hybrid layouts instead of
materializing padded cache regions.
- Preserves existing legacy paths for pure Mamba/SSM models, separate
K/V allocations, KV-transfer layouts, shared-backing layouts, and legacy
MLA paths.
- Adds optimized `gather_ssm_states` and `scatter_ssm_states_` Triton
kernels for non-contiguous Mamba state access.
- Documents and validates the supported state layout contract:
  - Only the first state stride may contain physical page padding.
  - Inner state dimensions must remain contiguous.
- State indices select physical rows and may be unsorted or
non-contiguous.
- `has_initial_state=False` produces a zero initial state without
reading the cache.

Generic advanced indexing is inefficient and unsafe for padded
non-contiguous state storage when used with the fused recurrent GDN
path.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No new user-facing CLI option is introduced.

The change is internal to Ascend KV cache allocation, layout
construction, and hybrid GDN state access.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Unit tests

- State gather/scatter correctness tests: 18 cases passed.
- MRV2 cache layout tests: 49 cases passed.
- Covered dense and padded layouts, block boundaries, multi-block tails,
`int32`/`int64` indices, real GDN state shapes, unselected rows, padding
preservation, empty-cache validation, and non-contiguous Attention K/V
views.

#### End-to-end model tests

- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B W8A8:
  - V1 engine.
  - ModelRunner V2.
  - FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph mode.
  - Short, long-context, repeated, and concurrent requests.
- Qwen2.5-7B GQA:
  - 28 attention heads and 4 KV heads.
  - Runtime logs confirmed non-contiguous K/V views.
- Short, long-context, repeated, and 32-way concurrent requests passed.
- All request matrix tests completed successfully with zero failed
requests.

#### GPQA Diamond accuracy

| Run | Correct / Total | Accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Before PR merge | 165 / 198 | 83.33% |
| After PR merge | 167 / 198 | 84.34% |

#### Performance before and after this PR

The pre-PR baseline used vLLM-Ascend commit
`af277b2681443089e4d29684b1101707e2eb6426` with Custom GDN operators.

The post-PR configuration used vLLM-Ascend commit
`fc4f6ffd97aafd7ad897c387031a46da05ce1d91` with FLA PR #559 operators
and non-contiguous KV cache.

Both configurations used:

- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B W8A8.
- TP=2 and EP.
- MTP=3.
- FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph mode.
- `fused_mc2=0`.
- `gpu_memory_utilization=0.90`.
- GSM8K full dataset: 1319 requests.
- Concurrency: 64.
- Maximum output length: 512 tokens.

Two opposite-order runs were completed:

| Run | Configuration | TTFT | TPOT | Output throughput | Total
throughput | Duration |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Pre-PR Custom | 627.1 ms | 35.8 ms | 1715.13 tok/s | 1954.16 tok/s
| 393.008 s |
| 2 | Post-PR FLA | 612.3 ms | 36.0 ms | 1702.93 tok/s | 1940.23 tok/s |
395.881 s |

#### State I/O ablation

Under the same FLA, model, graph mode, and non-contiguous layout:
| Run | Configuration | TTFT | TPOT | Output throughput | Total
throughput | Duration |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Old advanced-indexing path | 1491.2 ms | 87.8ms | 692.26 tok/s |
788.72 tok/s | 973.891 s |
| 2 | New gather/scatter path| 612.3 ms | 36.0 ms | 1702.93 tok/s |
1940.23 tok/s | 395.881 s |

The old advanced-indexing path caused both severe performance
degradation and abnormal early termination under the non-contiguous
layout.

#### Environment

- vLLM: `84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c`
- CANN: 9.2.0
- Ascend 910
- FLA
- TP=2, EP enabled
- `fused_mc2=0`
- FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph mode
- `gpu_memory_utilization=0.90`

### Related RFC

[RFC #17370](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/17370)
